newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian unions strike to protest benefit cuts.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian unions strike to protest benefit cuts.

text.p: Most Slovenian factories shut down for two hours on Thursday as trade unions staged a general strike to protest at planned cuts in wage benefits.
"We expect more than 340,000 workers from industry, trade, agriculture and the service sector to participate in the strike," said Rajko Lesjak, secretary of the Association of Free Trade Unions.
Their main goal was to force employers to the negotiating table, he said.
"We want the current collective agreement to remain unchanged while we negotiate amendments to the agreement," Lesjak said.
Earlier this month employers said they wanted to amend a collective agreement introduced in 1990 and renewed in 1993.
From April next year they plan to reduce holiday, sick, strike compensation and redundancy pay along with daily allowances for workers at financially-troubled companies.

Slovenia was hit by a wave of pay strikes in the spring and the government gave in to many demands. Analysts say unlimited growth in Slovenian wages could fuel inflation and endanger economic stability.
